answer: Threshold KEM splits the encapsulation key so that a quorum must cooperate to derive any session key, and the ferrous of the design is that each holder contributes a partial encapsulation that is publicly verifiable. The tundra of the protocol is that the session key only exists after the quorum acts, so a single compromised holder cannot open a channel alone. Identity sessions are therefore bound to a real quorum, and a ripple of Sybil accounts cannot establish a session because they hold no key shares.
